question: Can a fixed limited-coverage confidence alert allocate one retry better than random-all and verifier-first allocation?
old_study: generator-signals-v1 remains closed and failed; this is a different allocation question
candidate: unchanged saved decoded_confidence model and strict score > saved threshold

confirmation_gate.primary_uncertainty: one-sided 95% percentile multinomial puzzle bootstrap of TP/N - alert_fraction*failure_prevalence; lower > 0

capacity_floor_rationale: 2pp perfect-recovery capacity advantage over random-all would yield only 0.5pp advantage at uniform 25% recovery; this is a feasibility screen, not a measured utility claim or amended 40% recall gate
population: fixed 1600 never model-evaluated Sudoku Exchange project confirmation groups; checkpoint training exposure unknown

recovery.alternative_trigger: primary does not meet the actual recovery gate; evaluate the one predeclared alternative, then close
recovery.retention: keep original valid board; otherwise accept retry only if independently verified valid
recovery.replay: generate one potential retry for every confirmation puzzle, then evaluate policy allocations using paired potential outcomes; all experimental calls charged
recovery.allocation_budget: M = number of frozen alerts; random-all selects M puzzles, verifier-first selects M failures, each by fixed hash without retry outcomes
recovery.primary_comparison: confidence allocation minus expected verifier-first random-failure allocation at the same M retry count
recovery.random_baseline_expectation: exact conditional mean over uniform subsets of fixed size, plus one fixed-hash realized selection; no best random seed
recovery.confidence_interval: two-sided 97.5% paired puzzle percentile bootstrap, Bonferroni for two predeclared retry policies; lower > 0 against both random-all and verifier-first
recovery.resource_gate: common conservative sequential service-time envelope: N times mean monitored solve latency + M times the largest measured per-puzzle retry latency; each baseline gets as many worst-case retry slots as fit after N times mean plain solve latency, selecting by frozen hash without retry outcomes; confidence must still win. This is measured replay accounting, not a live hard-real-time controller
recovery.fallback_on_no_benefit: retain measured baseline results and close; no temperature/prefix/seed search

timing.order: alternate observed/plain then plain/observed, cycling the same first 8 already exposed calibration puzzles
timing.includes: boundary board reconstruction, confidence summaries, CPU feature extraction and saved linear score; synchronized full generator and final decoding
timing.claim: hardware-specific synchronized sequential service time, no production latency or speedup claim

stopping: one confirmation attempt; zero refits or threshold changes; incomplete/gate-failed confirmation permits only exposed-development feasibility alternative and closeout, never a fresh-confirmation claim
